n8n describes its model as fair-code/source-available and states that it does not call itself open source because the license limits use.
n8n documents Community edition feature boundaries separately from the code-license classification.
n8n documents Agent Builder and labels agent/self-hosted knowledge-base capabilities Preview with self-hosted queue-mode limitations.

The checked Loopmark repository LICENSE is MIT.
Loopmark scheduler source documents a local scheduler path and console error/status behavior, not managed retries or alerting.
Loopmark main history showed August 2026 packaging-related work; this did not independently verify a published package artifact tied to source.
Loopmark issues identify managed retry/alert and org/RBAC/post-approval work as planned items.
MarketingOS AI README presents a broader HubSpot-focused workspace and describes incomplete live persistence and production sync boundaries.
MarketingOS AI package manifest identifies a private 0.1.0 Next.js application and its declared dependencies.
MarketingOS AI main history showed four visible July 2026 commits; this is a limited maintenance signal, not a reliability assessment.
Mautic documents form actions that can send email, post elsewhere, or push contacts to integrations; the pilot leaves actions blank.
Mautic documents cron processing for queued marketing operations, which the proposed pilot keeps disabled.
Activepieces documents per-step run information, statuses, errors, checkpoints and retry/resume behavior; this supports a local review artifact, not alerting or approval guarantees.
The public Activepieces roles/permissions page labels RBAC as a paid feature, so granular CE pilot safeguards were not established from the checked material.
The Activepieces releases page showed 0.91.2 as Latest, published 23 September 2026; this is a dated release signal, not a reliability claim.
Marketing Agent OS source manifest names four pinned upstream snapshots; this audit did not independently compare every retained file or notice with each upstream commit.
Architecture describes selected-skill projection, excluded upstream snapshots, a lock record, hash material, and staged atomic replacement.

Security policy says optional helpers may run with local permissions, connectors may need credentials and inherit host/provider security, and authorization is required before external or persistent actions.
Compatibility documentation states target harness destinations and a 235-skill claim; this conflicts with the README 236-skill claim and does not prove target-harness runtime behavior.
Main history showed eight visible commits with the checked tip dated 4 September 2026; this is a point-in-time activity signal, not a quality or security result.
The Mautic 7.2.1 release record was labelled Latest on the research date; tag composer metadata declares GPL-3.0 for the checked repository package.
Mautic 7.2 documentation requires operator-provisioned campaign and queue or webhook processing commands; this does not establish that any deployment runs or supervises them.
Mautic documents granular roles, while the checked material did not establish immutable consent, dual approval, or least privilege in any deployment.
0.92.0 was released 24 September 2026; release notes mention job.failed logging and fixes but do not prove deployed reliability.
EE production use requires a commercial agreement; the checked license is on main, not the release tag.
The Manual Trigger piece page marks it MIT and every plan; the proposed 0.92.0 manual local flow was not executed.
Flow Approvals are Enterprise/Cloud with Environments and do not establish CE-enforced two-person review.
An interrupted in-flight step can run again before checkpoint, so external side effects are not exactly once.
The Compose guide requires preserving AP_ENCRYPTION_KEY with PostgreSQL backup for Connection recovery.
Current recovery docs name PostgreSQL and S3 systems of record and describe an acknowledged async webhook loss window if Redis data is lost.
Current unversioned Limits page states a 30-day self-host execution-data retention default and 50 MB run-log cap; deployed behavior is unverified.
Truncated Logs page still states 25 MB and differs from current Limits documentation.
Current environment reference lists UNSANDBOXED execution and UNRESTRICTED network defaults; deployed isolation was not tested.
Flow Approvals are Enterprise/Cloud with plan limits, not evidence of CE-enforced cross-product approval.
Interrupted in-flight work may run again before checkpoint; a target-side action requires separate reconciliation.
Campaign membership and event processing depend on operator-provisioned cron commands.
Skill instructions do not themselves authorize external or persistent actions; the host and operator own permissions.
The accessible v6.2.0 tagged Listmonk licence is AGPLv3 for the checked repository.
An open project request describes ongoing welcome behavior; checked documentation did not establish a built-in form/confirmation-to-welcome trigger.
A documented transactional API can be called by a separate actor; its presence does not establish an automatic welcome trigger.
Keila documents form-configured welcome after submission or double opt-in, with a download-link example; this behavior was not tested.
Current Keila core licence material states AGPL, but exact v0.30.3 licence and extra path scope were not directly readable.
Current extra notice excludes cloud-only code from the AGPL core grant; it does not establish exact v0.30.3 package scope.
Keila self-host configuration identifies PostgreSQL, upload persistence, secrets, and mail settings; a complete tested restore procedure was not established.
Mautic campaign processing requires operator-added cron commands, supporting the inference that it is a broader operating surface than one welcome message.
The v0.30.3 release identifies the exact commit used for this source audit.
The tagged README states AGPLv3-or-later except for the Keila logo and all files under extra/.
The exact tagged licence could not be read in this run; a cache miss is not evidence of absence.
The exact excluded-code notice could not be read in this run; scope remains open.
The tagged build file conditionally includes extra/ in compilation only when WITH_EXTRA is enabled and includes Oban.
The tagged Dockerfile declares build arguments and copies a release from builder to runtime; it does not prove the published image contents.
Docker Hub lists the 0.30.3 image and digest; the image and layer were not independently inspected.
Configuration identifies database, secrets, persisted uploads, mailer credentials and log settings, but no complete tested restore.
Cached security overview did not verify a current private disclosure route; this does not prove no route exists.
Managed-service bounce/complaint handling and optional self-hosted SES handling do not establish generic plain-SMTP outcome reconciliation.
Self-hosted sender options include SMTP and SES; managed Send with Keila is distinct.
Official release dates v6.2.0 and points to the checked commit.
Inspected double-opt-in handler selects unconfirmed memberships, confirms them, and renders a page without a distinct welcome send.
Checked core hook interface contains pre-confirmation SendOptinConfirmation, not a post-confirmation welcome hook.
Tagged system-template inventory lists the opt-in confirmation email, not a distinct welcome system email.
Confirmation SQL updates selected memberships and has no status predicate; concurrent unsubscribe race needs testing.
Transactional handler does not enforce confirmed membership, suppression or welcome-attempt idempotency; fallback/external can send without an existing subscriber.
Campaign recipient SQL distinguishes confirmed double-opt-in membership and exclusion, but a campaign is not a per-confirmation trigger.
Tagged repository licence is GNU AGPLv3 for checked code, not external providers or custom trigger.
Official v6.2.0 release identifies source commit, not installed artifact bytes or a digest in this workspace.
Confirmation handler selects unconfirmed memberships before update and page render; sequential duplicate and concurrent races require runtime testing.
Confirmation update lacks a status predicate; unsubscribe-between-read-and-update outcome is untested.
Public resubscription can reset unsubscribed list membership to unconfirmed while retaining confirmed membership.
Subscriber API documents global and per-list status and list/status filtering; a filtered read is not send authorization.
Inspected transactional handler does not provide welcome-specific consent, suppression or idempotency gates; no /api/tx call was made in this run.
Official release identifies v3.6.16, 26 May 2025 and short commit 69915ff; release provenance is not installed package verification.

Confirmation path reads prior confirmed status, writes confirmed/blacklisted/optedin fields, and conditionally calls sendMail with page-keyed confirmation text; send result and races are not resolved by those lines.
